name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: Griffith holds a roughly 20-to-1 fundraising advantage
Incumbent Griffith running after an easy renomination
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 2%
model.rationale: A 22-point Republican district, Griffith's roughly twenty-to-one money edge, and markets pricing a Democratic win at about two percent all point to a safe Republican hold, and no polls or ratings give any reason to move from that picture.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or an unusually large Democratic national wave, confirmed by unexpected polling, would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a southwest Virginia district that leans Republican by roughly twenty-two points. He has raised about $1.8 million and holds nearly $1 million on hand, while Democrat Joy Powers has raised about $85,000 with under $15,000 available. No public polls of the race have been conducted, and prediction markets give the Democrat roughly a two percent chance of winning.

The seat has been safely Republican in recent cycles, and Griffith was renominated without difficulty. Powers would need an extraordinary shift in the national environment or an unforeseen development in the district to become competitive. Absent such a change, the expected outcome is a comfortable Republican win by roughly nineteen points.
